### What the design identifies

```{r}
#| label: dag-structure
#| include: false
# causal structure from notes/04_analysis_plan.md §3b.4; adjustment sets and paths are quoted in the text
library(dagitty)
g <- dagitty('dag { X [exposure] Y [outcome] X -> Y }')
fmt_sets <- function(s) if (length(s) == 0) "none" else paste(sapply(s, \(v) paste0("{", paste(v, collapse = ", "), "}")), collapse = "; ")
```

The adjustment set for the effect of X on Y is `{r} fmt_sets(adjustmentSets(g, "X", "Y"))` …

### What this review fits

$$ \ldots $$

```{r}
#| label: fig-model-dags   # the fig- prefix is required: without it Quarto numbers every panel (a) and misplaces the caption
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-dpi: 150
#| layout-ncol: 2
#| fig-subcap:            # one short entry per program; without it Quarto repeats fig-cap under every panel
#|   - "<model>"
#| fig-cap: "The Bayesian models as graphs, one node per quantity of each Stan program: prior constants (yellow), parameters (green), derived quantities (grey), covariates (blue), data (red)."
source(here::here("lib/model_dag.R"))
nodes <- data.frame(name = c("h", "mu", "y"), label = c("N*'(0, 1)'", "mu", "y[i]"),
                    group = c("hyperparameter", "parameter", "observed"), x = c(0, 1, 2), y = c(1, 1, 1))
edges <- data.frame(from = c("h", "mu"), to = c("mu", "y"))
model_dag(nodes, edges, title = "<model>.stan")
```
